items.title: test(mcp): run MCP harness against an mcpchaos fleet and add ADM and EP test cases
items.body:
## Overview

The MCP harness now runs against a live mcpchaos fleet of upstream MCP servers instead of only exercising Bifrost on its own. This lets the harness cover client creation, STDIO and SSE transports, reconnects, tool refresh, and `/mcp` endpoint behavior against real upstream servers whose tools and sessions the tests control.

## Changes

- The harness runner (`run-newman-mcp-harness-tests.sh`) now builds `mcpchaos` from `tests/cmd/mcpconsole` and starts it with two placeholder servers, `alpha` and `beta`.
  - It waits for readiness, writes its log to the report directory, and stops it and removes its temp directory on exit.
  - It builds with `GOWORK=off` because the mock has its own module outside the repo workspace.
- The runner passes two new collection variables to Newman:
  - `chaos_url` is the fleet's base URL, used for both the MCP endpoints (`/s/<name>/mcp`, `/s/<name>/sse`) and the control API (`/control/...`).
  - `chaos_bin` is the binary that a STDIO client spawns to bridge to the fleet.
- New `--chaos-port` flag (default `8494`), with a port-in-use check like the existing one for Bifrost's port.
- In the Makefile, `run-mcp-harness-test` now takes `HARNESS_PORT` (previously `PORT`) and `CHAOS_PORT`.
- Each new test case resets the servers it uses through the control API (add the server, set its tools) and deletes the clients it creates, so cases don't depend on each other.
- New admin API cases:
  - **ADM-13:** create an HTTP client and read it back, checking the exact success body, `healthy` state, tool list, `is_ping_available`, and empty `vk_configs`.
  - **ADM-17:** create SSE and STDIO clients. It checks that both are healthy, that the STDIO client lists tools, that beta holds one session, and that alpha registers a STDIO pid.
  - **ADM-42:** reconnect a session-sticky client after the upstream kills its sessions, and confirm the upstream opened exactly one new session.
  - **ADM-44:** add a tool upstream, then confirm `refresh-tools` picks it up for both per-call and sticky clients (`tool_count` 3).
- New `/mcp` endpoint cases:
  - **EP-18:** `tools/call` success against the mock's echo, with upstream call counters checked.
  - **EP-23:** unknown tool returns `-32602`, and neither upstream receives a call.
  - **EP-27:** `ping` before `initialize` with numeric and string ids.
  - **EP-28:** client notifications and bare results return an empty `202`.
  - **EP-29:** unsupported methods (resources, prompts, logging, completion, unknown) return `-32601` with specific messages.
  - **EP-31:** content negotiation. A `text/plain` body, `Accept: text/event-stream` only, and no `Accept` header all get a plain JSON-RPC reply.
  - **EP-32:** no session id is issued or required, and a bogus `Mcp-Session-Id` is tolerated.
  - **EP-33:** `DELETE` and `PUT` on `/mcp` and `DELETE` on `/mcp/alpha` return `405` with `Allow: GET, OPTIONS, POST`.
- The existing ADM-62, ADM-73 and EP-09 cases are unchanged. They only move in the diff because the new cases were inserted before them.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

Requires Go and Newman (installed by the Make target). The run is hermetic: it boots its own Bifrost and mcpchaos fleet.

```sh
# Full harness, building tmp/bifrost-http from local code
make run-mcp-harness-test

# Run one folder only
make run-mcp-harness-test FOLDER="ADM-17"

# Use a prebuilt binary and custom ports
make run-mcp-harness-test BINARY=path/to/bifrost-http HARNESS_PORT=8093 CHAOS_PORT=8494
```

Expected: mcpchaos builds and reports ready on the chaos port, Bifrost boots, and all Newman folders pass. The mcpchaos log is written to the report directory.

New configuration:
- `HARNESS_PORT` (Make; maps to `--port`, default `8093`)
- `CHAOS_PORT` (Make; maps to `--chaos-port`, default `8494`)

## Screenshots/Recordings

N/A

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

This only affects the test tooling. Anyone invoking `make run-mcp-harness-test PORT=...` must switch to `HARNESS_PORT=...`.

## Related issues

N/A

## Security considerations

None. The mcpchaos fleet binds to `127.0.0.1` only, and the harness uses throwaway credentials and temp directories that are cleaned up on exit.

## Checklist

- [ ] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [ ] I updated documentation where needed
- [ ] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.title: test(mcp): add INF-05 Bedrock route e2e tests via mock LLM TLS listener
items.body:
## Summary Adds an end-to-end test for the Bedrock route (INF-05) to the MCP harness. It checks that Bedrock Converse and Converse-stream requests sent through Bifrost get MCP tools injected and return a `toolUse` from the mock LLM. The harness now has a Bedrock provider wired to the mock LLM. Bedrock clients only speak https to a bare host, so the provider reaches the mock through the fleet's TLS listener. ## Changes - Added the **INF-05 Bedrock route** folder to the `mcp-harness` Newman collection: - Setup registers a fresh mcpchaos server `alpha` (echo, add, greet) and a client `inf-05-alpha` with auth none and `tools_to_execute: ["*"]`, then scripts the mock LLM scenario `inf05` to answer with a `toolUse` for `alpha-echo`. - `converse` on `/bedrock/model/mock-model/converse` asserts that the response has exactly one `toolUse` named `alpha-echo` with id `tu1`. - `converse-stream` asserts that the response is `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` and opens exactly one `toolUse` named `alpha-echo`. - The mock LLM's request log must show two requests, one plain and one streamed (`bedrock.converse:false` and `bedrock.converse:true`). Both must declare `alpha-echo` as a toolSpec. - Teardown deletes the client. - Updated `run-newman-mcp-harness-tests.sh`: - Added a `--chaos-tls-port` option. It defaults to the chaos port + 1 and is checked for conflicts like the other ports. - mcpchaos now starts with `-tls-addr` and `-tls-server llm`, and the readiness check waits for both ports. - The generated Bifrost config includes a `bedrock` provider. Its runtime, control-plane and mantle endpoints all point at the TLS listener, and it sets `insecure_skip_verify` to accept the self-signed certificate. - Added `bedrock/mock-model` to the mock pricing datasheet. - Updated the header comments to describe the Bedrock path. - Design note: the TLS listener is a separate port on the same fleet, so the mock LLM logic is shared across all providers. Skipping certificate verification is limited to the test-only Bedrock provider config. ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Documentation - [x] Chore/CI ## Affected areas - [ ] Core (Go) - [ ] Transports (HTTP) - [x] Providers/Integrations - [ ] Plugins - [ ] UI (React) - [ ] Docs ## How to test Run the MCP harness with a built `bifrost-http` binary. Use `--folder` to run only the new scenario. ```sh # Run only the Bedrock scenario tests/e2e/api/runners/individual/run-newman-mcp-harness-tests.sh \ --binary /path/to/bifrost-http \ --folder "INF-05 Bedrock route" # Optionally choose ports explicitly tests/e2e/api/runners/individual/run-newman-mcp-harness-tests.sh \ --binary /path/to/bifrost-http \ --chaos-port 8494 --chaos-tls-port 8495 ``` Expected outcome: mcpchaos reports ready on both its plain and TLS ports. All INF-05 requests return 200, and the `toolUse` and request-log assertions pass. New option: `--chaos-tls-port

` sets the port for the fleet's TLS listener (default: chaos port + 1). ## Screenshots/Recordings N/A ## Breaking changes - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Related issues N/A ## Security considerations The Bedrock provider in the harness config sets `insecure_skip_verify: true` so it can trust the mock's self-signed certificate. This applies only to the local test configuration generated by the runner script. The mock runs on 127.0.0.1 and makes no external calls. ## Checklist - [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines - [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate - [ ] I updated documentation where needed - [ ] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI) - [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.title: test(mcp): add reply_error to chaosmock and load and upstream-capability harness tests
items.body:
## Summary

The chaos mock MCP server can now answer a tool call with a scripted JSON-RPC error. Before this, a scenario could only return a `CallToolResult` or trigger the faults the mock already produced. It could not return error codes that belong to a protocol revision, such as `-32021` (missing required client capability). The PR adds that ability and uses it in new end-to-end scenarios. It also adds load scenarios for the gateway and its upstreams.

## Changes

- Added a `reply_error` field to the mock tool definition. `tools/call` answers with the `{"code","message","data"}` object exactly as given.
- Validation rejects a `reply_error` that is not an object, is not a valid JSON-RPC error, or has a missing or zero code. It also rejects a tool that sets more than one of `reply`, `reply_error` and `reply_env`. The old two-way exclusivity check is now a check across all three sources. As with `reply`, a JSON `null` is treated as unset.
- Added a compat test showing that a real mcp-go client reads a scripted `-32021` error with its `data` intact, as a `MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError` naming `elicitation`, and that the call is counted once.
- Extended the control validation tests for the new rejection cases and updated the README tool-field table and rejection list.
- Added load scenarios to the MCP harness collection:
  - **GO-33:** 50 parallel `/mcp` sessions. Each session must get a unique session id, list tools and echo back its own argument. The scenario also checks that 50 log entries exist with the expected ids.
  - **GO-34:** 50 concurrent executes against a per-call client and against a sticky client. The per-call client must open 50 sessions, and the sticky client must open no new session or handshake.
  - **GO-35:** 200 `tools/call` requests on `/mcp` while `refresh-tools` runs 5 times.
  - **GO-36:** 50 concurrent executes over an SSE upstream, which must use one stream and one session.
- Added failure scenarios for upstreams that need what a user-facing client has:
  - **FAIL-27:** The upstream returns an `input_required` elicitation result. The scenario checks the 400 error text, the error log row and the `isError` result on `/mcp`.
  - **FAIL-28:** The upstream returns `-32021` naming the `elicitation` capability. The scenario checks that Bifrost reports the missing capability and does not retry.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

(Test tooling and coverage: this is closest to Chore/CI.)

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

(Only the test harness is touched: the `mcpconsole` chaos mock and the e2e API collection builder.)

## How to test

```sh
# Chaos mock unit and compat tests
go test ./tests/cmd/mcpconsole/chaosmock/...

# Regenerate the Postman collection, then run the GO-33 to GO-36, FAIL-27 and FAIL-28 folders
node tests/e2e/api/runners/build-mcp-harness.mjs
```

Expected results:
- The new `reply_error` validation cases return 400.
- `TestRealClientReadsAScriptedJSONRPCError` passes.
- The new harness folders pass against a running Bifrost with the chaos mock fleet.

Not applicable.

None. The change only affects the test mock and the e2e harness.

items.title: test(mcp): add e2e harness cases for library duplicates, installed flag, URL validation, and failure handling
items.body:
## Purpose

This PR adds end-to-end coverage to the MCP harness Postman collection (`tests/e2e/api/collections/mcp-harness.json`) for the MCP library and for failure handling. The library tests cover duplicate-name rejection, the `installed` flag, and config validation. The failure tests cover transport and tool-call errors.

## Changes

**MCP library (LIB)**
- **LIB-11 Duplicate names and slugs:** Publishing "My Server" a second time, publishing "my-server" (same slug), and publishing "Harness Catalog Server" (a boot catalog remote entry) must each return 409 with `an MCP library server with this name already exists`. A control request first confirms the remote entry is live.
- **LIB-18 Installed flag by URL:** A library entry reports `installed: false` until a client exists at its URL. A client at the same URL with a trailing `/` and a different name flips it to `true`.
- **LIB-19 Installed flag by name, rename, delete:**
  - The entry goes `false`, then `true` after a client named `chaos_alpha` is created.
  - The client's `endpoint_slug` is `chaos-alpha`.
  - Renaming the client to `lib19_renamed` keeps both the slug and `installed: true`.
  - Deleting the client returns the entry to `installed: false`.
- **LIB-20 Installed flag for STDIO:** A STDIO entry is `installed: true` when a STDIO client has identical args, and stays `false` when the args differ (a different mcpchaos server).
- **LIB-32 / LIB-33 URL scheme validation:** `PUT /api/config` with a `file://` or `ftp://` `mcp_library_url` returns 400. The `file://` case checks the error mentions `config.json` and that the stored URL is unchanged. The `ftp://` case checks for `only https and http schemes are allowed, got: ftp`.
- **LIB-37 Valid interval:** `mcp_library_sync_interval` of 7200 is accepted and reads back as 7200. The original value is restored in teardown.

**Failure handling (FAIL)** — a new `FAIL Failure handling` group:
- **FAIL-02:** Creating an SSE client against a closed port returns 500 with `failed to start MCP client transport after 5 retries`. The response is expected to take between 30s and 40s.
- **FAIL-14:** `refresh-tools` while `tools/list` fails returns 500 with `Failed to refresh MCP client tools: failed to list tools for MCP client alpha` in under 7s. The client stays `healthy`.
- **FAIL-16:** Per-call (non-sticky) clients ignore session kills. After the kill, executing a tool opens exactly one new session.
- **FAIL-18:** A malformed `tools/call` reply returns 400 with `MCP tool call failed for alpha-echo_tool`. Alpha receives exactly one call, and a control call to `add_tool` still succeeds.

**Notes**
- Every folder cleans up after itself by deleting the entries and clients it creates. The LIB-37 folder also restores the sync interval it changes.
- The existing LOG tests (LOG-27 through LOG-41) are unchanged. They now sit after the new LIB folders, and the FAIL group follows them.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

Run the MCP harness collection against a gateway with dashboard auth enabled, the admin credentials set, and the mcpchaos fleet reachable at `chaos_url`.

```sh
# Core/Transports
go version
go test ./...

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

Expected: all new LIB-11, LIB-18, LIB-19, LIB-20, LIB-32, LIB-33, LIB-37, FAIL-02, FAIL-14, FAIL-16 and FAIL-18 requests pass. FAIL-02 intentionally takes about 30s.

The collection relies on these variables: `base_url`, `admin_auth_header`, `chaos_url` and `chaos_bin`. The STDIO test in LIB-20 needs `chaos_bin` to point at the mcpchaos binary.

## Screenshots/Recordings

Not applicable (no UI changes).

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

N/A

## Security considerations

None. The tests use local addresses (`127.0.0.1:9`) and the mcpchaos fleet. They also check that `file://` and `ftp://` library URLs are rejected over the config API.

items.title: fix(mcp): keep tls_config on per_user_headers clients so servers behind a custom CA verify
items.body:
## Summary Fixes creation of `per_user_headers` MCP clients that connect to a server behind a custom CA. The add-client handler dropped `tls_config` for this auth type, so verification dialed without the CA certificate and failed. This PR forwards `tls_config` for these clients. It also adds a TLS listener to the `mcpchaos` test fleet, so the case can be tested end to end. ## Changes - Fixed `addMCPClient` in the HTTP transport handler so a `per_user_headers` client keeps its `tls_config`. The same config is used for verification, the runtime, and the stored client. - Added a handler unit test, `TestAddMCPClient_PerUserHeadersKeepsTLSConfig`. It checks that the config reaches both the manager and the config store. - Added an optional HTTPS listener to the `mcpchaos` fleet, enabled with `-tls-addr `. - It serves the same fleet, including `/s//mcp`. - It uses a self-signed loopback certificate generated at startup (ECDSA P-256, valid for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`). - It shuts down gracefully together with the main listener. - `GET /control` now returns `tls_url` and `tls_cert_pem` when the TLS listener is open, so tests can trust the certificate as a custom CA. - Added `TestServeTLSServesTheFleetUnderS`. It checks that a client trusting the reported certificate can initialize against `/s/alpha/mcp`, and that a client without it refuses the connection. - Added the e2e Newman case **AUTH-51** (per_user_headers over TLS with a custom CA) to the MCP harness. It reads the TLS URL and certificate from `/control`, creates a client with `ca_cert_pem`, opens and submits a header flow, executes a tool, and checks the call ran under the submitted key's identity. - Updated the harness runner script: - New `--chaos-tls-port` flag, defaulting to the fleet port + 1. - A check that the TLS port is free. - The readiness wait now covers both ports. - Documented the TLS listener and the new `/control` fields in the chaosmock README and the `mcpchaos` usage comment. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Documentation - [x] Chore/CI ## Affected areas - [x] Core (Go) - [x] Transports (HTTP) - [ ] Providers/Integrations - [ ] Plugins - [ ] UI (React) - [ ] Docs ## How to test Run the handler and chaosmock tests: ```sh # Core/Transports go version go test ./transports/bifrost-http/handlers/ -run TestAddMCPClient_PerUserHeadersKeepsTLSConfig cd tests/cmd/mcpconsole && go test ./chaosmock/ -run TestServeTLS ``` Try the TLS listener manually: ```sh ./tmp/mcpchaos -servers alpha -tls-addr 127.0.0.1:8401 curl localhost:8400/control # includes tls_url and tls_cert_pem ``` Run the e2e AUTH-51 case: ```sh tests/e2e/api/runners/individual/run-newman-mcp-harness-tests.sh --binary --folder "AUTH-51" ``` Expected: the client registers with 2 tools discovered, the header flow completes, and the tool call runs under `key-a`'s identity. New option: `--chaos-tls-port

` on the runner script (defaults to the chaos port + 1). ## Screenshots/Recordings N/A ## Breaking changes - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Related issues N/A ## Security considerations - `tls_config` (including a custom CA) is now honored for `per_user_headers` clients, so verification uses the supplied CA rather than failing. Certificate verification is not disabled. - The mock's certificate is self-signed and generated in memory at startup. It is only for the test fleet and is exposed through its control endpoint. ## Checklist - [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines - [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate - [x] I updated documentation where needed - [ ] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI) - [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.title: feat(mcpconsole/chaosmock): add legacy HTTP+SSE transport to the chaos mock server
items.body:
## Overview

Adds the legacy HTTP+SSE transport to the chaosmock MCP fixture, so clients can be tested against both transports instead of assuming the two behave alike. Streamable HTTP returns a response in the reply to the POST. Legacy SSE acknowledges the POST with 202 and delivers the response on a separately opened stream. That difference changes what a dropped connection means: under streamable HTTP it fails the request in flight, while under SSE it strands the request, because the POST already succeeded and the answer has nowhere to land.

## Changes

- Added `ServeSSE` and `ServeSSEMessage` in a new `sse.go`, routed at `/s/<name>/sse` and `/s/<name>/sse/message`. The stream open creates the session, and the `endpoint` event carries the session id for later POSTs.
- Added `Fleet.SSEURL(name)`. The message endpoint is deliberately not exposed, since a client should learn it from the `endpoint` event.
- The `endpoint` event is built from the request's own path (`r.URL.Path + "/message?session=..."`) rather than a bare relative reference. A relative `message` would resolve to `/s/alpha/message` instead of extending the path. Deriving it from the request also keeps the same-origin check valid however the fleet is addressed.
- Existing fault injection applies to the SSE endpoints. Refuse, injected HTTP status, session kill and malformed-body faults are all supported. A malformed body is delivered on the stream, and an injected HTTP failure answers on the POST because there is no JSON-RPC message to carry it.
- `handleInitialize` now reuses a session the caller already holds instead of always minting one. Under streamable HTTP `initialize` creates the session, but under SSE the stream already created it. Minting unconditionally would double-count sessions and leave the client addressing a session the server no longer routes responses to. A new `sessionStore.negotiated` records the negotiated protocol version under the store lock.
- The stream registry now holds two kinds of stream:
  - Anonymous streams are for the streamable HTTP listening stream.
  - Keyed streams are addressed by session id and used for SSE.
  - Added `addKeyed`, which replaces and closes a displaced stream, and `send`, which delivers to one session's stream.
  - `remove`, `broadcast`, `closeAll` and `count` cover both kinds.
- The README now documents both transports and the stranded-request behavior.
- Added `sse_test.go`, which runs the real `mcp-go` SSE client against the mock. It covers:
  - handshake and tool listing
  - tool calls and dispatch counters
  - tool mutation between lists
  - a dropped stream stranding a request until the caller's own deadline
  - an injected 503 on stream open creating no session

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
# Core/Transports
go version
go test ./tests/cmd/mcpconsole/chaosmock/...
```

Expected: all tests pass, including the new `TestSSE*` cases. In `TestSSEDroppedStreamStrandsTheRequest`, the `tools/list` call made after `DropStreams()` returns an error once its own deadline expires and does not hang.

No new configs or environment variables are required.

## Screenshots/Recordings

N/A, no UI changes.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

N/A

## Security considerations

The SSE stream endpoint applies the same bearer-auth check as the existing mock endpoints. SSE message bodies are capped at 1 MiB. This is a test fixture and is not intended for production use.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [x] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.title: test(mcp): add governance e2e tests for virtual MCPs and virtual keys
items.body:
## Overview

Adds a "GOV Governance" folder to the MCP e2e harness Postman collection (`tests/e2e/api/collections/mcp-harness.json`). It covers virtual MCP and virtual key governance behavior that had no end-to-end coverage. Each scenario brings up a fresh mcpchaos server `alpha` (echo, add, greet), registers it as a client, runs its checks, and deletes everything it created.

## Changes

- **GOV-06, legacy `allow_on_all_virtual_keys`:**
  - Checks that sending `true` on create or update sets both `allow_by_default` and `allow_on_all_virtual_keys`.
  - Checks that an explicit `allow_by_default: false` wins over `allow_on_all_virtual_keys: true` on both create and update.
- **GOV-11, grants edited from the client side:**
  - A VK with no MCP configs gets 403 on `alpha-add`.
  - After a `PUT` with `vk_configs` granting `["add"]`, `alpha-add` returns 200 and `alpha-echo` still returns 403.
  - An empty `virtual_key_id` and a repeated `virtual_key_id` are both rejected with 400.
- **GOV-16, unknown VK value:** `x-bf-vk: sk-bf-doesnotexist` returns 401 with type `access_not_found` and the expected message on tool execute, and 401 on `/mcp` initialize.
- **GOV-17, VK required:**
  - With `enforce_auth_on_inference` enabled and no credential, tool execute returns 401 with type `virtual_key_required` and the expected message.
  - The test reads the current client config first and restores it in teardown so later tests are unaffected.
- **GOV-29, virtual MCP create:**
  - Creating "Tools A" over alpha's `echo` yields slug `tools-a`, `enabled: true`, and empty `virtual_key_ids`.
  - A missing name, malformed JSON, and an unknown MCP client id (`invalid MCP client IDs: x`) each return 400.
- **GOV-31, virtual MCP update and lookup:**
  - A `PUT` with a new slug leaves the slug as `tools-a`.
  - A `PUT` without `tools` preserves the existing tools.
  - `enabled: false` persists on a subsequent GET.
  - A non-numeric id returns 400 and an unknown id returns 404.
- **GOV-32, attach and detach VKs:**
  - Attaching an unknown VK returns 404, and detaching a VK that was never attached returns 200.
  - Attaching the same VK twice succeeds and lists it once.

items.title: feat(tests/mcpconsole): add control API and mcpchaos command for chaos mock MCP server fleet
items.body:
## Overview

Adds the HTTP control API to `chaosmock`, plus a standalone `mcpchaos` command that runs a fleet of controllable mock MCP servers. A scenario can now change a server's tools, credentials and failure behaviour while an MCP client stays connected, then compare what the client reports against the counters the server kept.

## Changes

- Added the control API in `chaosmock/control.go`, mounted on the fleet at `/control` and `/control/<name>/...`.
  - Fleet level: `GET /control` returns every server's state plus connection stats, and `POST /control` with `add` or `remove` adds or removes a server.
  - Per server, tool verbs: add, remove, set, rename, describe, schema and per-identity overlay.
  - Per server, failure and auth verbs: faults and faults/clear, auth, auth/grant and auth/revoke.
  - Per server, session and stream verbs: sessions/kill, streams/drop, notify/tools-changed and counters/reset.
- Every mutating verb returns the server's state after the change, so a scenario step reads as its own record in a transcript. The state includes tools, revision, faults, auth, counters, live session count and live stream count.
- Unknown verbs and unknown JSON fields return 400. A typo that silently did nothing would look the same as the system under test behaving correctly.
- The overlay verb has an explicit `clear` flag. Removing an overlay returns an identity to the base tool set, while an empty overlay shows that identity no tools.
- Added `cmd/mcpchaos`, which starts a fleet from `-servers` and `-tools` or from a `-seed` JSON file.
  - The seed file can define per-identity tool views, auth and starting faults, and rejects unknown fields.
  - The command prints the MCP and control URLs for each server and shuts down cleanly on SIGINT or SIGTERM.
- Added a README covering the following:
  - why the protocol is hand-rolled, so the mock can violate it on demand;
  - the control verbs;
  - faults grouped by the layer they break at;
  - what each counter can prove;
  - why session count rather than connection count is the HTTP reconnect signal, since mcp-go clients share `http.DefaultTransport`;
  - how push notifications reach only clients that opted into continuous listening.
- Added `control_test.go`, which covers:
  - tool mutations, including that a rename preserves the description and that the revision advances;
  - 400 on unknown verbs and unknown fields;
  - faults taking effect on a live client, and recovering after being cleared;
  - counter reset keeping live sessions;
  - fleet add/remove, where a removed server returns 404 instead of refusing the connection.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

This change is limited to the test tooling under `tests/cmd/mcpconsole`.

## How to test

```sh
cd tests/cmd/mcpconsole

# Run the chaosmock tests, including the new control API tests
GOWORK=off go test ./chaosmock/ -race

# Build and run the fleet
GOWORK=off go build -o ./tmp/mcpchaos ./cmd/mcpchaos
./tmp/mcpchaos -servers alpha,beta -tools echo_tool,add_tool

# In another terminal
curl localhost:8400/control
curl -XPOST localhost:8400/control/alpha/tools/add -d '{"tool":{"name":"new_tool"}}'
curl -XPOST localhost:8400/control/alpha/faults -d '{"faults":{"status":429}}'
curl -XPOST localhost:8400/control/alpha/faults/clear
```

Expected: the tests pass, each control call returns the updated server state, and an unknown verb or field returns 400.

New flags on `mcpchaos`:
- `-addr` (default `127.0.0.1:8400`)
- `-servers` (default `alpha`)
- `-tools` (default `echo_tool,add_tool`)
- `-seed` (path to a JSON file; overrides `-servers` and `-tools`)

## Screenshots/Recordings

Not applicable.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

None.

## Security considerations

The control API is unauthenticated and can change server behaviour, so it is intended for local test use only. `mcpchaos` binds to `127.0.0.1` by default, and it should not be exposed on a shared or public interface.

items.title: test(mcp): add e2e API tests for client read encodings and PUT patch semantics
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds two end-to-end API scenarios to the MCP harness Postman collection. They cover how the MCP client admin API returns stored fields on read, and how `PUT` handles partial updates and immutable fields. Both scenarios run against a fresh mcpchaos server (`alpha`) serving `echo_tool` and `add_tool`.

## Changes

- **ADM-14 Stored fields come back in read encodings**
  - Creates a client with headers, `tool_sync_interval` 5, `tool_execution_timeout` 30 and `allow_by_default` true, then sets `tool_pricing` with a `PUT`.
  - Reads the client back and checks that:
    - The header value is redacted, keeping the first and last four characters (`abcd****…****ijkl`).
    - `tool_sync_interval` is returned as `300000000000`.
    - `tool_execution_timeout` is returned as `"30s"`.
    - `allow_on_all_virtual_keys` is `true`.
    - `tool_pricing` is echoed as `{ echo_tool: 0.25 }`.
  - Teardown clears the pricing and deletes the client.

- **ADM-47 PUT is a patch and ignores immutable fields**
  - Creates a client with headers, `tools_to_execute` and `tools_to_auto_execute`, sets pricing with a `PUT`, and saves the config read-back in a collection variable.
  - Sends a `PUT` with `name`, `connection_string`, `auth_type` and `endpoint_slug`, and expects "MCP client edited successfully".
  - Reads the client again and asserts that:
    - Only `name` changed. The rest of the config equals the earlier read.
    - Both tools (`add_tool`, `echo_tool`) are still listed.
  - Teardown clears the pricing and deletes the client.

- **Design notes**
  - Each scenario is self-contained: it sets up its own chaos server and client, and cleans up after itself.
  - The pricing is cleared before deletion in both scenarios.
  - The ADM-47 comparison deletes `name` from both sides and compares the rest with a deep-equal. This catches any unintended change to other fields.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

Run the MCP harness Postman collection (`tests/e2e/api/collections/mcp-harness.json`) against a running gateway and an mcpchaos server. Make sure `base_url`, `chaos_url` and `admin_auth_header` are set. The ADM-14 and ADM-47 folders should pass in full.

```sh
# Core/Transports
go version
go test ./...

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

No new configs or environment variables are introduced.

## Screenshots/Recordings

N/A (no UI changes).

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

N/A

## Security considerations

The ADM-14 scenario asserts that header values are redacted on read, so secrets are not returned in plaintext. The ADM-47 scenario asserts that `PUT` cannot change immutable fields such as `connection_string`, `auth_type` and `endpoint_slug`.

items.title: test(mcp): add SYNC e2e harness tests for upstream tool changes across every client type
items.body:
## Overview

Adds a new `SYNC Tool sync` section to the MCP e2e harness (`tests/e2e/api/runners/build-mcp-harness.mjs`). It checks that a client with `per_user_discovery` off picks up upstream tool changes and exposes them correctly on every route a caller uses. Until now, no case covered how a changed upstream tool list reaches callers across the different client types.

## Changes

- Every SYNC case makes the same upstream change: `new_tool` is added and `add_tool` is removed. Exactly one of three mechanisms is then allowed to pick it up:
  - **Sync interval:** `tool_sync_interval` set to 5s. The case polls the client listing and asserts the change appears within 20s.
  - **`tools/list_changed` push:** the client syncs every 10m, so only the push can update it. The case asserts that one open stream exists, then checks the change within 5s. This runs only for sticky clients, since a per-call client holds no connection to hear the push.
  - **`POST /api/mcp/client/{id}/refresh-tools`:** the client syncs every 10m. The case checks that the listing is unchanged before the call, that the call reports 2 tools, and that the listing is updated afterwards.
- The cases run across 12 client types. These are HTTP with auth none, headers and shared OAuth, each per call and sticky; HTTP `per_user_headers` and `per_user_oauth`; SSE with none, headers and shared OAuth; and STDIO. Together with the three mechanisms this produces one case per valid combination.
- After the change, each case checks the same routes as a VK that is granted every tool of the client and attached to a Virtual MCP:
  - The client listing.
  - `tools/list` and `tools/call` on `/mcp`, on the slug endpoint `/mcp/{client}`, and on the Virtual MCP endpoint `/mcp/{client}-vmcp`. `new_tool` must run and `add_tool` must be refused.
  - The execute API.
  - The tools offered to the model in a chat completion, captured from the mock LLM.
  - After the client is switched to code mode, `getToolDocs` and `executeToolCode`.
- The mock's counters are checked as well. `tools/list` must be asked again, and for sticky interval cases a ping must be seen too. For per-user types the count is taken under the client's own admin identity, and tool calls are attributed to the caller's identity. `new_tool` must have run 5 times and `add_tool` never.
- Per-user clients are signed in first, through the header flow or the OAuth flow. OAuth cases restore the config at teardown.
- Design notes:
  - The gateway endpoints re-register a client's tools in the background after its list changes, so those checks poll `tools/list` every 200ms for up to 5s instead of asserting once.
  - Code mode is switched on last because it rebinds stored tools without asking the upstream.
- Not covered: OpenAPI clients, whose tools come from a stored spec, and per-user auth types over SSE or STDIO, which Bifrost refuses (CONN-19).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)

This change only touches the e2e API test harness.

## How to test

Regenerate the collection from the builder script and run it against a Bifrost instance with the chaos MCP fleet and mock LLM. The new `SYNC Tool sync` section should pass for every client type and mechanism.

```sh
# Core/Transports
go version
go test ./...

# UI
cd ui
pnpm i || npm i
pnpm test || npm test
pnpm build || npm run build
```

No new configs or environment variables are required.

Not applicable, no UI changes.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

None linked.

## Security considerations

No production code changes. The tests use mock credentials only (`x-key` values, mock OAuth identities) against the local chaos server.
